stage_2_story.text_en:
Moshe and his son Avi sat down together on Friday night to watch Maccabi Tel Aviv take on their biggest rival in the EuroLeague. Avi loves basketball and has been playing since he was a teenager. He was happy to explain the tactics to his father.

The game began at a furious pace. In the first quarter, Maccabi fell behind after a series of poor turnovers. Avi explained: 'Abba, when we lose possession like that, the other team gets a fast break — they run before our defence is ready and get an easy basket.'

But Maccabi's coach called a timeout and the team regrouped. In the second quarter they started using the pick-and-roll much more effectively. The guard would receive a screen, use a sharp crossover to beat his man, and either attack the rim himself or find an open teammate.

The third quarter was Maccabi's best. Their top defender made three steals and turned each one into points on the fast break. Their centre also produced a thunderous block that sent the ball into the stands. Maccabi moved the ball quickly through transition and built a twelve-point lead.

Hapoel clawed back in the fourth quarter by slowing possession down and being patient. But Maccabi held on. Moshe turned to Avi at the final buzzer and said: 'So, if they keep the ball and don't rush, they win. Is that the secret?' Avi laughed. 'That's one of the secrets, Abba.'
